title: dedicated: autoscaler token-bucket smoothing + burst reporting improvements
author: Amit Rao
description: Context: customers running Dedicated fleets observed short-lived burst spikes causing throttling and noisy utilization reporting. The autoscaler token-bucket currently allows instantaneous bursts but the smoothing behavior leads to noisy reported utilization and oscillations in scale decisions. This PR introduces a token-bucket smoothing policy (configurable), improves utilization metrics emitted by the fleet controller, and adds a reporting layer that exposes smoothed and raw utilization for easier incident analysis. Changes include: 1) implement exponential smoothing of token-bucket refill/consume rates with a per-fleet configurable alpha; 2) expose prometheus metrics redwood_fleet_utilization_raw, redwood_fleet_utilization_smoothed, redwood_tokenbucket_available; 3) add a burst_controller that enforces burst_duration and burst_tokens with new safety guards to avoid sustained overcommit; 4) update autoscaler reconciliation loop to use smoothed rates for scale decisions while retaining raw metrics for alerts and post-mortem; 5) add integration tests simulating bursty traffic and a canary in the dedicated-autoscaler helm chart; 6) docs and operator notes for tuning smoothing alpha and burst caps. Motivation: reduce scale thrashing during short bursts and give operators better visibility into both instantaneous and trend utilization. Checklist: - [x] Impl smoothing algorithm and config surface - [x] Metric names and tagging for per-fleet breakdown - [x] Integration tests covering common burst patterns - [x] Added e2e smoke to release pipeline - [x] Docs and changelog entry - [x] Security review (no secrets exposure) Backwards compatibility: smoothing defaults to alpha=1.0 (no smoothing) so existing behavior unchanged unless operators enable smoothing. Rolling upgrade safe across controller versions.
commits: Initial impl: tokenbucket smoothing and metric hooks
Autoscaler: use smoothed utilization for scale decision; preserve raw metrics
Tests: add integration test harness for bursty traffic; flake fixes
Docs: operator tuning guide and changelog entry
Tweaks: tighten burst safety checks and add feature flag
review_comments: Priya Shah: Great work, the smoothing approach looks sound. A couple of nit comments on the alpha default and telemetry tags. Can we make per-tenant override opt-in?
Amit Rao: Answered - made per-fleet override behind feature flag and left default alpha=1.0 to preserve behavior. Added tests for enabling per-fleet smoothing.
Jon Kim: Observability changes look good. Request: include high-cardinality tag safeguards (fleet_id only) and document retention expectations.
Amit Rao: Added telemetry guard to avoid adding customer-specific tags to high-frequency metrics and updated docs section on retention.
Ellen Brooks: Integration test flaked on first run (timing), some assertions were brittle. After tightening timings tests are stable. Approve.
CI: integration tests failed on first pipeline run due to race in tokenbucket refill. Fixed by atomically updating refill counters. Reran CI: all green.
release_notes:
- Added token-bucket smoothing to dedicated autoscaler (configurable per-fleet)
- New metrics: redwood_fleet_utilization_raw, redwood_fleet_utilization_smoothed, redwood_tokenbucket_available
- Safety guards for burst controls to prevent sustained overcommit
- Operator docs: tuning guide for smoothing alpha and burst caps
